title: ELSS: Understanding Equity Linked Saving Scheme Funds & Tax Benefits

faq.q: What is the minimum investment amount for ELSS?
faq.a: Most ELSS funds allow you to start investing with as little as ₹500, especially through Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs).

faq.q: Can I invest in ELSS through SIP?
faq.a: Yes, you can invest in ELSS through SIPs. Each SIP instalment will have its own three-year lock-in period from the date of investment.
ELSS funds invest primarily in equities, making them subject to market risks. While they offer potential for high returns, there is also a risk of capital loss, similar to other equity mutual funds.

faq.q: What happens after the 3-year lock-in period?
faq.a: After the three-year lock-in, your ELSS units become free for redemption. You can choose to redeem them, switch to another fund, or continue holding them for further growth.

faq.q: Are the returns from ELSS taxable?
faq.a: Yes, long-term capital gains (LTCG) from ELSS exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year are taxed at 10% without indexation. Dividends are taxed as per your income slab.

faq.q: How does ELSS compare to PPF for tax saving?
faq.a: ELSS offers potential for higher, market-linked returns with a 3-year lock-in, but carries market risk. PPF offers guaranteed, fixed returns with a 15-year lock-in and is considered very low risk.
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can invest in ELSS funds, provided they comply with FEMA regulations and complete KYC formalities. However, NRIs residing in certain countries may have restrictions.
